text: Innkeeper: “Anything else you want to ask?”
Innkeeper: “Glad she's awake. Her wound still needs time. Take it slow on the road.”
Innkeeper: He sets down the cloth he was wiping the sword with and glances toward the table.
Innkeeper: “You're awake. She's breathing steadily, but she won't wake.”
Innkeeper: He looks up, the cloth still in his hand.
Innkeeper: “Looking for the young woman you came with? She's by that table.”
“What happened to her? Can you help?”
Innkeeper: “You can still use the medicine chest. Find out what she took first. I'll stay clear and let you handle it.”

Innkeeper: “She collapsed in the night. I didn't dare give her anything. That guest was acting strangely. Try the single room upstairs by the steps, the one with the door open. You might find something. The medicine chest is on my right. Once you know what she took, I can bandage her.”
“What exactly happened last night?”

Innkeeper: “She came down and made it as far as the table before she fell. Her old wound was bleeding badly. That guest demanded I hand her over. I refused. We drew swords, and he cut my hand. He left before things got any worse.
Innkeeper: Some of the blood on this sword got there when I caught her. I saw her reach under the table before she fell, but I didn't see what she put there.”
“Did you give her something that did this to her?”
Innkeeper: “She came to me for the disguise medicine herself. I told her what it was. Ask her when she wakes if you doubt me. For now, help her. The chest is unlocked.”
“Step back. I'll get the medicine. Don't touch her again.”
Innkeeper: He lets go and takes half a step back.
Innkeeper: “All right. I won't touch her. The chest is on the right. Follow the notes you brought, and make sure you use the right medicine.”
“Which came first, the meal or the disguise medicine?”

Innkeeper: “The meal. She bought the disguise medicine from me afterward. It was later still when the guest noticed something was missing. He didn't recognize her face, but he noticed her clothes and kept asking about the blonde guest.
Innkeeper: I didn't see him slip anything into her food. I can't say which bite did it.”
“Did the people in that old ledger all go with you willingly?”
Innkeeper: He folds the cloth, then folds it again.
Innkeeper: “One didn't. I handed them over anyway. Later I heard they'd been locked up. After that, nothing. I don't know what became of them.

Innkeeper: Later I let someone else go. It cost that guest money and made me an enemy of my employer. I left the trade, but I never got entirely clear of it. Saying I was keeping my end of a bargain won't cover it up.”
“She asked for the disguise herself. I was too quick to judge.”
Innkeeper: “You went back and checked. That's something. It doesn't clean up my past. Take her with you.”
“The road isn't safe. Let's talk about that sword.”
